investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC only: curl (plain HTTP GET, descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser/JS execution) against the venue's official '/agenda' listing page (Webflow) and one linked event detail page.

probe_history.reason: A plain curl GET of https://www.cabaretsauvage.com/agenda immediately exposed a Webflow CMS Collection List (class="w-dyn-list"/"w-dyn-item") rendered as plain static HTML, with ~120 dated cards (class="post-date") each carrying a weekday+date badge, a title, a category, and its own canonical URL. A second plain GET of one linked detail page (Tony Vega) confirmed title/date/price/door-time directly, but also surfaced a genuine internal date inconsistency (see field_assessment.start_date) — sufficient to complete the investigation without further escalation, though not sufficient to establish start_date as a trustworthy PROVEN fact for this source.

venue_reference: Cabaret Sauvage (concert/club/festival venue, 59 Boulevard Macdonald, 75019 Paris — Parc de la Villette)

identity.notes: Retained page's own <title> reads 'Cabaret Sauvage | Agenda' at the venue's own domain cabaretsauvage.com. The sitewide footer states '59 Bd Macdonald / 75019 Paris', matching the venue's known address, and all media assets are self-hosted under Webflow's own CDN (cdn.prod.website-files.com) for this one site.

site_classification.platform: Webflow — event cards are rendered server-side/statically as CMS Collection List items ('w-dyn-item'/'w-dyn-list'), not fetched client-side; no schema.org JSON-LD is present anywhere sampled. Ticketing is delegated to an informal Linktree ('linktr.ee/cabaretsauvagebilletterie') rather than a dedicated ticketing-platform integration, and at least one individual event's own 'Points de vente' field names a ticket-reseller domain ('Ticketmas.com') that does not match any recognised, canonical ticketing brand — noted honestly as a further data-quality concern, not verified further (out of scope, and no claim is made about that domain's legitimacy either way).

title.notes: The listing card's own work-title text, confirmed identical on the event's own detail page heading (h1.heading-4).

start_date.notes: A genuine, retained, first-party CONTRADICTION was found on this event's own official detail page, not merely a missing-context gap: the page's own hero badge states 'MER 04.11.26' (matching the listing card's own 'post-date' badge, also 'MER 04.11.26', and the page's own body sentence 'mercredi 4 novembre' — three mutually consistent DIRECT statements), while a separately-labelled 'Date :' field on the SAME page states '11/5/2026' in an unstated numeric format. A mechanical Gregorian weekday check (not model judgement) shows neither reading of '11/5/2026' resolves the conflict in the majority's favour: 5 November 2026 falls on a Thursday and 11 May 2026 falls on a Monday, and NEITHER is the Wednesday ('MER') the other three signals agree on and independently verify. Because this is a direct contradiction between two first-party fields (not a gap DETERMINISTIC_CONTEXT could fill), and resolving it in favour of the majority would require a plausibility judgement this policy classifies as AI_INFERENCE, start_date is recorded honestly as AMBIGUOUS rather than PROVEN for this sampled record. This also raises a broader per-record data-quality concern about this source that a future collector would need to handle explicitly (e.g. flagging or discarding records with internally conflicting date fields) rather than silently trusting either value at scale.

time.notes: A door-opening time ('Ouverture des portes : 19:00') is stated on the detail page, but since the very date this time would attach to is itself unresolved (AMBIGUOUS, see start_date) for this sampled record, and this is a door time rather than a confirmed performance start time, it stays PARTIAL rather than PROVEN.

end.notes: No end time or end date is stated anywhere on either sampled page.

venue_location.value: Cabaret Sauvage, 59 Boulevard Macdonald, 75019 Paris (Parc de la Villette)
venue_location.notes: Neither sampled page repeats a full venue name+address directly beside the event card itself, but this is mechanically determinable: the site is a dedicated single-venue domain with no other venue ever named, and its sitewide footer states the address directly, unchanged across both sampled pages.

derivation.rule: every event card and detail page on this dedicated single-venue domain belongs to the one venue named in that domain's own sitewide footer; concatenate the site's own footer address with that implied venue identity to get each event's venue_location
inputs: site is a single-venue dedicated domain (cabaretsauvage.com) with no other venue referenced anywhere sampled
sitewide footer states '59 Bd Macdonald / 75019 Paris' identically on the listing and detail page

source_record_id.notes: The event's own Webflow CMS slug ('/work/tony-vega'), used as this source's own canonical path — the same documented judgement as tempodrom-berlin-01/le-trabendo-paris-01. This is independent of the start_date ambiguity above; the slug itself is unambiguous.

event_url.notes: The card's own href, confirmed to resolve to the detail page sampled.

price.notes: The detail page directly states 'Tarifs : 55€'. This value is independent of, and unaffected by, the start_date ambiguity above.

blockers.description: At least one sampled record (Tony Vega) carries two directly-stated, mutually-inconsistent date values on its own official detail page (a weekday-consistent hero/list badge vs. a differently-formatted 'Date:' field), with no source-declared rule resolving the conflict. A collector cannot safely trust either the list-page badge or the detail-page 'Date:' field for every record without per-record human verification or a validated cross-check rule, undermining reliable automated start_date acquisition at scale for this source specifically.

Ticketing is delegated to an informal Linktree link rather than a dedicated ticketing platform, and at least one sampled record names a ticket-reseller domain ('Ticketmas.com') that does not match any recognised canonical ticketing brand — a further signal of lighter editorial/technical quality control on this venue's own site relative to the other three Paris venues investigated in this same batch.

reasons: Identity PROVEN and a genuine public STATIC_HTML acquisition path exists (Webflow CMS Collection List, CONFIRMED public data paths on both the listing and one detail page).
title, source_record_id, event_url, and price all PROVEN with basis DIRECT_SOURCE — these facts are independently reliable.

However, start_date — one of the two fields this policy treats as essential for activation — could only be assessed as AMBIGUOUS, not PROVEN, because the one sampled event's own official detail page contains two directly-stated, mutually-contradictory date values, cross-checked mechanically (Gregorian weekday computation) against a third, independently-consistent signal (the listing card's own badge). Resolving this in favour of the majority would require a plausibility judgement this policy classifies as AI_INFERENCE, which can never be the basis of a PROVEN field.

This is a genuine, retained, first-party data-quality problem specific to this source (not a technical acquisition blocker) — it needs a human decision about whether/how to handle per-record date conflicts (e.g. discarding conflicting records, requiring manual confirmation, or determining whether this is rare or systematic across the venue's ~120 listed events) before any collector is built or any activation is considered, rather than an AI investigator unilaterally picking a side or discarding an otherwise largely-usable source.

Combined with the informal Linktree ticketing delegation and one observed non-canonical-looking ticket-reseller domain, this venue's overall data-provenance profile is honestly weaker than the other three Paris venues investigated in this same batch, matching the concern flagged at task assignment.
No collector code was written for this investigation, per this project's own instruction to only proceed with ingestion work when a decision reaches READY_FOR_OFFLINE_PROOF or READY_FOR_ACTIVATION.
